candidate_ledger.output_variable_reasoning: The Nusselt number (Nu) is a dimensionless quantity representing the ratio of convective to conductive heat transfer across a fluid layer. It is derived from the given physical quantities related to the Rayleigh-Bénard convection problem, which include length (h), temperature difference (delta_T), thermal conductivity (lambda), gravitational acceleration (g), thermal expansion coefficient (alpha), kinematic viscosity (nu), and thermal diffusivity (kappa). Since Nu is dimensionless, all SI exponents are zero.

variables.physical_definition: Height of the fluid container or layer.
Temperature difference between the top and bottom surfaces of the fluid layer.
Thermal conductivity of the fluid, representing the ability to conduct heat.
Gravitational acceleration acting on the fluid.
Thermal expansion coefficient, measuring fractional decrease in fluid density per unit temperature increase at constant pressure.
Kinematic viscosity of the fluid, representing momentum diffusivity.
Thermal diffusivity of the fluid, representing thermal energy diffusivity.
